canonical.idPolicy: Harness-assigned opaque 8-character IDs: collision-checked deterministic SHA256/base64url prefixes map EACH WHOLE generated structured bunch ID bijectively. Counters, run grouping, operation order, anchors and characters are identical to the structured replay. Not recorded collaborator identities; no refresh or regrouping.

source.attribution: Editing trace by Martin Kleppmann and the paper's authors, from automerge/automerge-perf. The upstream README states CC-BY-4.0 for the trace. Its concurrent history was flattened to index-based single-character edits; cursor moves are omitted.

upstreamVerification.method: Local operation/text digests match pinned upstream JSON-literal comparison

methodology.scope: Numerical-container experiment only, not a complete IdList, ID lookup benchmark, editor or Mongo storage claim. Strings remain opaque eight-character IDs. Same F05 JSON in every case; flat vs paged topology is a separate factor from numeric representation.
methodology.representation: Each page owns bunchId string references, signed counts, explicit reconstructed start counters, and Map<string,row-index-array>. A flat directory and cumulative visible-length prefix index cover pages. Ordinary uses JS small-integer arrays for all numeric arrays; typed32 (typed-all) uses Int32 counts plus Uint32 starts, map row indexes, and prefixes. Dense-only uses typed counts/starts/prefix but keeps ordinary small row-index arrays. This separates dense-column optimization from thousands of tiny typed-buffer wrappers.
methodology.loading: Fetch excluded. JSON parse plus complete validation, sparse-counter reconstruction, page allocation, all typed conversions and index building are timed. Parse+initialize TOTAL is the outcome; conversion breakdown is diagnostic, not a reason to reject cheap translation that benefits runtime memory/editing. Parsed source references disappear when load returns, before GC. No original JSON retained. Cold creation in a fresh browser process per trial; no p95 claims from three editing trials/six loads per configuration.
methodology.editing: 2,000 deterministic whole-run visibility toggles, not character edits. Every mutation copies the affected count array, page object, flat page directory and prefix array, updating later prefix entries. Unchanged strings, start counters and identity maps are shared. History maintenance is timed. No forced GC inside the timed loop; common workload generation and observable checksums/verification are outside it.
methodology.memory: Prepared-page baseline precedes load. Three consecutive after-GC heap+backing observations at each stage preserve raw ranges; 8MiB buffer calibration rejects double counting backing bytes. No workload/expected arrays retained between calls. History is 100 prior numeric-container versions only. Current state and three retained old versions are checked before memory observations. Memory ranges show collection noise, not confidence intervals or peak allocation.
methodology.widths: Both representations deliberately enforce the same narrow domain: nonzero signed counts with magnitude <=2^31−1; start counters, end counters, row indexes, total visible length and prefixes <=2^32−1. Values outside this domain are rejected, never silently truncated. Production needs a validated Float64/safe-number fallback or wider representation; this probe does not implement it.
methodology.limitations: No insertion, split/merge, counter mutation, new-string growth, persistent balanced-tree update or rendering is exercised. This is not proof that replacing NativeF05 columns by typed arrays has identical overall results. Retained memory includes small row-index arrays and maps; not all numeric arrays are large columns. Keep all trials, including outliers.
